Theme

Latin word

quis

quis (sī quis, nē quis)

pronoun, indefinite, declension

one, anyone (after sī, nisi, nē, num); someone, anyone (after sī, nisi, num, nē); who?

In this lexicon

  • one

    also used · classical · Petr. 34.1: sī quis nostrum iterum vellet mulsum sūmere

  • someone

    also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 83: sī quis deus mihi largiātur; Cic. Amic. 88: sī quis in caelum ascendisset

  • who

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Men. 137: Quis homō est?; Catull. 1.1: cui dōnō lepidum novum libellum?; Traupman 406

  • quis sit: identity

    classical

  • Nōn quis sed quid.: it’s not who you are but what you are that counts

    modern

  • nesciō quis, nesciō quid: someone

    classical

Examples

  • sī quis nostrum iterum vellet mulsum sūmere

    if any of us wanted another glass of honeyed winePetr. 34.1

    In the entry for one

  • sī quis in caelum ascendisset nātūramque mundī et pulchritūdinem sīderum perspexisset, īnsuāvem illam admīrātiōnem eī fore; quae jūcundissima fuisset, sī aliquem cui narrāret habuisset

    if someone went up into heaven and saw the nature of the universe and the beauty of the stars, the wonder of it would give him no pleasure; it would have been the sweetest thing if he had had someone to tellCic. Amic. 88

    In the entry for someone

  • Quis homō est? — Ego sum.

    Who’s there? — It’s me.Plaut. Men. 137–137b

    In the entry for who

  • Manē, manē. quis illīc est?

    Wait, wait. Who’s that over there?Plaut. Aul. 655

    In the entry for who

  • cui dōnō lepidum novum libellum āridā modo pūmice expolītum?

    to whom shall I give my charming new little book, just polished with dry pumice?Catull. 1.1–2

    In the entry for who

  • quem fugis, āh dēmēns?

    whom are you running from, you madman?Verg. E. 2.60

    In the entry for who

  • ‘ante’ inquit ‘circumspiciendum est cum quibus edās et bibās quam quid edās et bibās’

    “look first,” he says, “at whom you eat and drink with, then at what you eat and drink”Sen. Ep. 19.10

    In the entry for who

  • Quis tū homō es?

    Who are you?Traupman 111

    In the entry for who

  • Quibuscum?

    With whom?Traupman 41

    In the entry for who
